newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - April 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - April 14.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- FORD TO CUT COSTS WITH 'VIRTUAL' ASSEMBLY LINES

The U.S.'s second-biggest car maker, Ford, is set to introduce "virtual" assembly lines which use advanced computer technology to test production layouts on screen. The technology allows Ford to test new assembly lines for practicality and efficiency by showing virtual workers on the line and also "virtually" assemble cars using 3D parts and computer animation. The breakthrough system is hoped to cut 120 million stg off development costs for new models, as virtual cars can now be built on the virtual assembly line.
-- BANKS CUT RATES IN EMERGING MARKETS

Competition among banks in Western Europe for business in emerging markets is helping borrowers in Eastern Europe and North Africa who wish to obtain syndicated loans at rates closer to those in Western Europe. While rates in some eastern countries are falling, interest rates are said to be exceptionally tight. Many western bankers have chosen to look abroad for business, after loan rates have fallen so far in increased competition that some are reluctant to become involved.
-- BT MOVE ENDS PHONE BILL MARK-UPS BY SMALL HOTELS

British Telecommunications is about to withdraw a service to calculate call charges in thousands of small and medium-sized hotels, which will result in the elimination of substantial mark-ups on guests' phone bills. Unless adjustments are made in hotels, they will no longer be able to monitor or cost guests' outgoing calls. Hotel calls are said to represent the third largest source of income for smaller hotel businesses. The move by BT comes as a result of ongoing hotel industry pressure.
-- GLOBALISATION UNDERLIES CHEMICAL INDUSTRY WOES

The chemical industry in Britain is currently facing uncertainty as falling output and a strong pound beset the export-dependent sector. Hopes that Britain would become a world leader in the industry just a year ago have been dashed as it continues to struggle with strong global competition and has been forced itself to become global in order to achieve growth. The industry faces competition from manufacturers from Japan, Taiwan, Korea and China.
-- SHARP RISE PLANNED IN TV SET OUTPUT

Heavy investment from Asian TV manufacturers of about one billion stg on TV plant expansion in Britain has prompted predictions of a large rise in TV set production again this year. One in three TVs manufactured in the EU is made in Britain compared with one in five in 1990. Currently, 6.2 million TV sets are produced each year in Britain according to the British Radio and Electronic Equipment Manufacturers' Association, two-thirds of which are exported.
-- BT'S 2.3 MILLION STG INVESTORS SET TO GIVE VERDICT ON MCI DEAL

By Tuesday BT will know whether its 2.3 million stg investors have agreed to the merger with the U.S.'s MCI.The meeting will be held at Wembley Conference Centre to decide on the deal which could form the Concert plc. Seventy-seven percent of BT's equity is held by big institutional investors who are not expected to intervene at this stage of the merger. Shareholders of MCI backed the proposal two weeks ago. However, approval is still required by the EC and US regulators but a favorable decision is expected within a few weeks and the end of summer respectively.
-- AVONMORE'S WATERFORD BID TARGETS FARMERS

On Sunday Irish foods company Avonmore launched an offer for Waterford Foods of nearly 290 million Irish pounds (276 million stg) to shareholders and farmers in the Co-operative that controls the target. The one-for-two share offer values Waterford shares at 117.5p at Avonmore's closing price on Friday. The target is for a co-operative to own 67 percent of the business which, should the merger take place, would create the largest milk company in Ireland and the UK.
-- BARDON AND CAMAS TO CEMENT MERGER

Midland-based building materials companies Bardon and Camas are set to announce a merger as soon as today, creating one of the largest companies in the UK with sales on excess of 725 million stg. The two companies combined hold a stockmarket price of almost 200 million stg. Negotiations for a merger took place last year but fell through due to the inability to agree on a management plan. The two companies account for 10 percent of UK aggregates market and more than 10 percent of road buildings and repairs. If the merger takes place then it would be the latest rationalisation move within the industry which reduces competition and allows companies to increase prices.
-- SATELLITE OPERATION INDUSTRY SET 'TO TRIPLE'

A study by the US finance house Merrill Lynch predicts that satellite operations will triple from 4.5 billion dollars in 1996 to 14.7 billion dollars by 2002 and if home television services are included it will rise to 31 billion dollars. Merrill Lynch experts expect the main method of delivering advanced digital telephony, fixed and mobile, high-speed Internet access, and multi-channel digital television will be satelite communications over the next four year period.
